chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Aṣbagh ibn al-Aṣbagh, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, from Marwān ibn Muslim, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah or Burayd al-ʿIjlī—the doubt is from Muḥammad—who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A bondwoman committed zina. He said, “She is to be lashed fifty lashes.” I said: If she repeats it? He said, “She is to be lashed fifty.” I said: Is rajm upon her in any circumstance? He said, “If she commits zina eight times, rajm becomes obligatory upon her.” I said: How did it become so in eight times? He said, “Because the free person, if he commits zina four times and the hadd is carried out upon him, he is killed. So when the bondwoman commits zina eight times, she is stoned on the ninth.” I said: What is the reason for that? He said, “Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had mercy on her and did not combine upon her the yoke of bondage and the hadd of a free person.” He said: Then he said, “It is upon the Imam of the Muslims to pay her price to her masters from the share of the riqāb.”

key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: stoning as a legal hadd punishment
key_terms.الْحُرُّ: a free person, in contrast to a bondwoman
key_terms.رِبْقَ الرِّقِّ: the yoke or burden of bondage
key_terms.سَهْمِ الرِّقَابِ: the allocated share for freeing slaves or matters related to bondage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a bondwoman who repeatedly commits zina in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a legal ruling concerning the hadd for a bondwoman who commits zina, stating that her punishment is half that of a free person and explaining when rajm applies after repeated offenses. It also states that the Imam of the Muslims must compensate her owners from the share allocated to riqāb, showing the legal and administrative dimensions of the ruling.
